title: Why you're taller in the morning than at night, by almost 1 cm
description:
Why your height changes during the day: under load, your spinal discs lose fluid and compress, then recover overnight. Find out when to measure your height so the numbers are honest.
#shorts #height #spine #humanbody #science

scenes.narration: You're taller in the morning. And you can prove it.
scenes.imagePrompt: cinematic shot of a person standing against a wall height chart in soft blue morning light, shallow depth of field, dark teal palette

scenes.narration: Over a day, you get shorter by about a centimeter on average. Some people lose more, some less.
scenes.imagePrompt: macro close-up of a measuring tape glowing under cold blue light, dark background, cinematic rim light

scenes.narration: Your tape measure isn't lying. Your spinal discs, the soft cushions between your vertebrae, are getting squeezed.
scenes.imagePrompt: glowing translucent human spine model floating in darkness, soft cyan light between vertebrae, cinematic macro

scenes.narration: All day you stand, walk, carry bags. Under that load, the discs lose fluid and get thinner.
scenes.imagePrompt: crowd of commuters walking with heavy bags on a city street at dusk, motion blur, cool blue and amber tones, cinematic

scenes.narration: At night you lie down, and the load is gone. The discs soak up fluid again, and by morning your height is back.
scenes.imagePrompt: person sleeping peacefully in a dark bedroom lit by soft moonlight from a window, calm teal palette, cinematic wide shot

scenes.narration: Researchers Reilly, Tyrrell and Troup measured this back in the eighties. The difference can reach about one percent of your height.
scenes.imagePrompt: 1980s research lab with a scientist writing measurements in a notebook, warm desk lamp against blue shadows, cinematic

scenes.narration: So here's the takeaway. Measure your height in the morning. Compare measurements taken at the same time of day.
scenes.imagePrompt: pencil height marks on a wooden door frame in early morning light, soft blue shadows, shallow depth of field

scenes.narration: Astronauts in space get taller too. It's the same mechanism, just without gravity.
scenes.imagePrompt: astronaut floating inside a space station module, Earth glowing through the window, cool blue cinematic lighting

scenes.narration: Have you ever noticed you're shorter at night? Tell me in the comments.
